constraints.groupingRule: First screen shows parent modules only; files remain evidence links inside each node.

summary.role: Freehand is a Rust-first agent runtime with typed contracts, provider adapters, durable reason/task truth, WebUI/Android/ACP surfaces, Relay transport, and architecture gates.
summary.primaryFlow: Client surface -> typed UI protocol -> runtime bridge -> reason engine -> provider adapter -> external model API; tool and task results re-enter the same owner-owned loop before projection.

nodes.name: Config & Registry
nodes.role: Owns TOML config parsing, validation, agent topology, provider/model selection, remote daemon registry, safe projections, and account-config sync.
nodes.dataFlow: Reads ~/.freehand/config.toml, compiles selected agent/provider/peer/remote-route truth, and exposes redacted projections to runtime and UI.
nodes.impact: Invalid or mutated configuration stops bootstrap or marks changes restart-required; it never leaks credentials into UI payloads.

nodes.name: Shared Contracts
nodes.role: Defines cross-module IDs, typed request/context/provider/tool/error contracts, preview contracts, usage, and serialization truth.
nodes.dataFlow: Carries semantic data between owners without allowing one module's internal control state to become another module's payload.
nodes.impact: Contract drift breaks compilation or cross-crate replay; these types are the common language of every flow.

nodes.name: Instruction Loader
nodes.role: Discovers, validates, compiles, fingerprints, and renders AGENTS/skill capability manifests before model-visible admission.
nodes.dataFlow: Scans declared instruction roots into a deterministic manifest; the context planner admits only rendered typed capability segments.
nodes.impact: Prevents runtime/UI/provider crates from independently scanning or mutating instruction authoring surfaces.

nodes.name: Reason Turn Engine
nodes.role: Owns turn state, provider-output application, completion schema, tool re-entry, persistence, session history, and terminal projection.
nodes.dataFlow: Turn input becomes durable turn truth; provider/tool outputs are applied through typed gates until a valid terminal boundary.
nodes.impact: This is the only owner allowed to mutate session/turn truth; app surfaces only consume projections.

nodes.name: Provider Semantics
nodes.role: Defines provider-neutral requests, tools, hosted search, semantic events, errors, usage, and adapter mapping.
nodes.dataFlow: Semantic request -> family-specific wire adapter -> provider events -> normalized semantic output/errors.
nodes.impact: Keeps OpenAI and Anthropic wire formats out of runtime/reason while preserving raw event semantics.

nodes.name: OpenAI Adapter
nodes.role: Renders/parses Responses and Chat Completions wire formats and executes streaming/non-streaming OpenAI-compatible requests.
nodes.dataFlow: Semantic request -> OpenAI JSON/SSE; provider events return through provider-core normalization.
nodes.impact: Wire drift is isolated here; runtime never sees provider DTO internals.

nodes.name: Anthropic Adapter
nodes.role: Renders/parses Anthropic Messages requests and executes single-shot/streaming Anthropic-compatible traffic.
nodes.dataFlow: Semantic request -> Messages JSON/SSE; tool-use, usage, hosted search, and errors normalize through provider-core.
nodes.impact: Keeps Anthropic protocol behavior in one owner and prevents semantic payload rewriting elsewhere.

nodes.name: Tool Registry & Execution
nodes.role: Owns built-in schemas, role-specific exposure, locked-workspace execution, previews, web fetch, and tool output semantics.
nodes.dataFlow: Typed tool call -> schema/scope validation -> preview when mutable -> execution result paired back into the reason loop.
nodes.impact: All built-in model tools execute here; app/reason code must not invent duplicate tool execution.

nodes.name: Runtime Orchestration
nodes.role: Composes config/provider/reason/tool/task/node truth, dispatches UI commands, runs Master/Worker loops, retries provider work, and coordinates checkpoints.
nodes.dataFlow: Typed command -> owner dispatch -> live reason/tool loop -> durable task/turn/debug state -> protocol projections.
nodes.impact: This is the central orchestration boundary; semantic helpers belong in owners, not here.

nodes.name: Task & Agent Lifecycle
nodes.role: Owns durable tasks, assignments, executions, reviews, leases, AgentBoard snapshots, EventInbox, and worker controls.
nodes.dataFlow: Task mutation -> ledger + snapshot -> scheduler/lifecycle projection; restart recovery rebuilds from authoritative files.
nodes.impact: Task completion and Worker takeover decisions must read this owner, not UI text or process state alone.

nodes.name: UI Protocol
nodes.role: Validates commands, separates ingress/query/subscribe, builds owner-routing envelopes, and projects UI state without owning business truth.
nodes.dataFlow: UI command -> validation/envelope -> runtime; owner truth returns as typed query, subscription, or turn projection.
nodes.impact: WebUI, Android, CLI, and headless tests share one protocol instead of local browser/session state.

nodes.name: WebUI Server Surface
nodes.role: Hosts protocol-driven WebUI assets, HTTP query/SSE mirrors, ADP WebSocket command/query/subscribe, health, and Android update routes.
nodes.dataFlow: Static shell loads once; live state flows through versioned ADP WebSocket with SSE as a latest-turn display mirror.
nodes.impact: The browser never owns session/task truth and cannot bypass runtime dispatch.

nodes.name: Daemon Host & Services
nodes.role: Selects Master/Worker/Relay modes, validates local ADP auth, hosts transports, supervises launchd lifetime, and wires runtime adapters.
nodes.dataFlow: Env/config -> selected mode -> guarded process -> WebUI/ADP listener -> injected runtime dispatcher.
nodes.impact: A daemon owns service lifetime only; business truth remains in reason/task/config owners.

nodes.name: Relay Transport & Updates
nodes.role: Owns account auth, Agent directory/presence, control/data/error tunnels, HTTP/ADP proxy, update manifests, and APK bytes.
nodes.dataFlow: Authenticated control tunnel admits data/error channels; remote clients proxy to the selected daemon without rewriting payload semantics.
nodes.impact: Relay is endpoint/account transport, not task/session truth; updates must preserve hash/signer identity.

nodes.name: Node Pairing & Directory
nodes.role: Compiles reciprocal Master/Worker topology, validates pairing, owns remote daemon directory snapshots and direct/Relay route selection.
nodes.dataFlow: Config registry -> node directory -> selected route; pairing identity gates delegated task/direct-message traffic.
nodes.impact: Topology is config-owned; runtime must not synthesize peer IDs or bypass route selection.

nodes.name: Android Client
nodes.role: Thin WebView host plus connection profiles, APK update checks/downloads, file permissions, notifications, and Android Back bridge.
nodes.dataFlow: Loads daemon-hosted WebUI at `?client=android-webview`; native code only bridges platform capabilities and installer handoff.
nodes.impact: Product UI stays canonical WebUI; Android never recreates conversation/settings/update business logic.

nodes.name: Workspace Gates & Release
nodes.role: Owns CI/build/release, resource-map/function-map/mainline gates, source-search boundaries, OpenMinis lifecycle evidence, and release/install scripts.
nodes.dataFlow: Source/docs changes -> mainline/gate checks -> build/test/release artifacts -> install scripts -> live service/device verification.
nodes.impact: Architecture and release claims require executable gate evidence; generated/runtime outputs are not implementation search truth.

nodes.name: Metadata, Debug & Error Center
nodes.role: Owns watermarked metadata admission, debug snapshots/sinks, control status parsing, and centralized error classification/recovery decisions.
nodes.dataFlow: Owner events -> typed metadata/debug/error contracts -> durable ledgers or UI-safe projections; request text never enters control metadata.
nodes.impact: Control/debug/error state cannot leak into provider payload or be silently stripped from the error chain.
